messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-T3 - high connection waiters on postgres-write-01 and redis-main (region-us-west). Auto-escalation scheduled in 5m unless acked. Links: https://pd.company.example/incidents/PD-T3-5210001111
PagerDuty Bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-T3-5210001111 — triggered by threshold: pg.waiters > 50, redis.maxclients > 3900
Elliot (oncall): acked. I'm on it. pulling logs and runbook now.
Julia (oncall): I'm available for handoff if needed. tagging @Matt and @Ash.
Ash (sre): seeing a big spike in redis used connections from inference-warmers, and pg waiting backpressure on write pool. Some clients show repeated CONNECTs from the inference-gateway swarm.
Matt (db): jumping in. PG activity: >60 waiters, most from pgbouncer pool 'inference-writers'. Query waiters show lots of small insert/upserts into usage_metrics.
Kei (platform): deploy-bot shows a rolling canary for inference-worker v2.3 started ~10m ago. Could be cache-warmers ramping traffic.
Elliot (oncall): impact? any 5xx or customer-facing slowdowns yet?
Ash (sre): API gateway errors increasing; 95th latency spiking from 200ms -> 1.2s on text-generation endpoints. Some customers seeing throttles. No widespread 5xx yet but retry noise.
Julia (oncall): customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants in us-west reported throttling in support queue. Not large scale but degrading SLAs for some customers.
Matt (db): immediate mitigation plan from db runbook: 1) reduce writer traffic to PG by enabling write circuit-breaker in gateway 2) increase pgbouncer pool temporarily 3) throttle cache-warmers.
Elliot (oncall): let's run it. Kei, can you flip the gateway circuit-breaker for writes to 10rps per client id for 5m? Add a header to route non-critical fill jobs to degraded queue.
Kei (platform): I can toggle rate-limiter rule w/ this command:

```
infractl gateway patch-rate-limit --service inference-api --rule "write_fillers" --limit 10/s --scope client_id --ttl 300
```

Applying now.
deploy-bot: Can confirm traffic replay from canary: inference-worker/2.3 heat-up produced 2.5x more concurrent cache fills.
Ash (sre): also I'm going to flip the cache-filler flag off on the canary instances via feature-flag.
Elliot (oncall): Matt, increase pgbouncer max_client_conn and reserve some server pools?
Matt (db): bumping pgbouncer `max_client_conn` from 5000 -> 8000 on pgbouncer-write-01 and pgbouncer-write-02, and increasing per-user pool_size for inference-writers from 100 -> 200. Restarting pgbouncer gracefully one node at a time.

```
# pgbouncer.ini snippet
pool_mode = session
max_client_conn = 8000
default_pool_size = 100
[databases]
redwood = host=postgres-write-01 dbname=redwood
```

Matt (db): restarting pgbouncer-write-01 now (rolling), will wait for drain.
Ash (sre): I've disabled the cache-warmer flag for the canary group. That should stop churn into Redis.
Elliot (oncall): Redis status?
Ash (sre): redis-main maxclients peaked at 3998, now dropping to ~1800 after toggles. Eviction rate spiked; we're seeing higher latency on GETs but acceptable.
Julia (oncall): customer impact: support ticket 10213 from Tenant:trinity reports longer response time, ticket updated with mitigation steps.
Kei (platform): gateway rule applied, confirmed: write_fillers rate-limited for canary client_ids.
Matt (db): pgbouncer-write-01 restarted and back to service. Waiters dropped from 68 -> 12 within ~40s.
Elliot (oncall): good. keep monitoring 2m intervals. who will own post-mortem if this turns into an incident?
Julia (oncall): I'll take incident lead if PD escalates. For now I'll collect affected tenants and timeline.
Ash (sre): adding monitoring graphs: https://grafana.company.example/d/pg-redis/pg-redis-waiters?orgId=1&from=-30m
Elliot (oncall): any root cause hypothesis?
Matt (db): early hypothesis: simultaneous canary boot + cache warmers generated a thundering herd of short-lived connections to Redis and a burst of writes to PG metrics table. Two backpressure loops collided: Redis accept queue -> retry -> more PG writes.
Kei (platform): will add a guardrail in our deploy process: delay cache-filler ramp by 2 minutes after canary launch and introduce jitter for connector warm-ups.
Ash (sre): ops checklist done: - rate limit applied - cache-warmer disabled - pgbouncer scaled and restarted - monitoring pinned
Elliot (oncall): PD incident remains acknowledged; auto-escalation cancelled.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident PD-T3-5210001111 acknowledged by Elliot (oncall) at 5210001123. Auto-escalation cancelled.
Julia (oncall): handoff plan: I'll stay on for next 30m, then hand back to Ash for follow-up. Julia -> Ash.
Ash (sre): will follow up with a remediation ticket to add deploy gating and add a pre-warm circuit-breaker. Assigning to @Kei and @Matt.
Matt (db): also proposing a DB-side circuit-breaker: queue writes into a buffer when waiters > 30 to avoid pgbouncer saturation.
Kei (platform): noted. I'll open infra PR and add deploy delay flag to canary pipeline.
Elliot (oncall): final notes for post-incident: collect timing of toggles, pgbouncer logs, redis INFO stats during window, list of tenants affected and retry logs from gateway.
Julia (oncall): I'll create the incident doc + timeline and tag this thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Elliot (oncall): nice quick mitigation. moving to monitoring state. if anything flares, re-open PD.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment paused by platform: inference-worker/2.3
Ash (sre): closing loop: current 95p latency back to 230ms, redis connections stable ~600, pgbouncer waiters <5. Marking resolved-but-followup.
Julia (oncall): incident doc: https://docs.company.example/incidents/PD-T3-5210001111
Elliot (oncall): handover complete to Julia. ending thread.
notes: short-hand real-time coordination: apply circuit-breakers, rate-limits, pgbouncer bump, disable cache-warmers, canary pause; prepare postmortem
